name: Sharp Face Avoidance and Cube Addition for Maximum Classes
statement: If $H$ is maximum of rank $r\ge1$, a maximum rank-$(r-1)$ subclass avoiding a prescribed section on a fixed block $D$ exists exactly when $|D|\ge r$. Dually, if $M$ is maximum of rank $R<|Z|$, a maximum rank-$(R+1)$ class containing $M$ and any positioned $t$-cube exists exactly when $t\le R+1$.
proof: Necessity for avoidance follows because the $D$-reduction of a rank-$(r-1)$ maximum class is nonempty when $|D|<r$. For sufficiency, reduce one fixed coordinate, recursively choose a lower-rank avoiding subclass, and lift the reduction on the opposite shore and the subclass on the prescribed shore; Pascal gives maximumity. Complementation turns avoidance of the fixed face of a positioned cube into the cube-addition statement.
